description: A worklist algorithm that converts an ε-free NFA to an equivalent DFA, where each DFA state is a frozenset of NFA states. Demonstrated on an NFA for strings ending in 'ba'.
source: draft: opencode free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `subset_construction` takes an NFA dict with `start` (frozenset), `accept` (frozenset), and `delta` mapping `(state, symbol)` to frozensets. `worklist` holds subsets to process, `visited` tracks seen subsets, and `dfa_states` maps each frozenset to its transition dict.

The main loop pops a `current_set` from the worklist. Lines 16-20 collect the alphabet: for each NFA state in the set, it scans `nfa["delta"]` for transitions originating from that state and adds the symbol to `alphabet`.

For each symbol in the alphabet, it builds `next_set` as the frozenset of all `s2` reachable from any `s1` in `current_set` on that symbol. If `next_set` is non-empty, it records the transition in `dfa_states` and adds `next_set` to the worklist if unseen.

steps.answer: The DFA state `{q0, q1}` is created. From there, on `a`: `q0` goes to `q0` and `q1` goes to `q2`, so the next set is `{q0, q2}`. That set contains the accepting state `q2`, so it becomes an accepting DFA state.
steps.question: The NFA `ENDS_IN_BA_NFA` has three states `q0`, `q1`, `q2`. The start set is `{q0}`. On `b` from `q0` the NFA goes to `{q0, q1}`. What DFA state does this create, and what happens on `a` from that state?

steps.description: `dfa_accept` collects every DFA state (frozenset) whose intersection with `nfa["accept"]` is non-empty. A DFA state accepts if any NFA state in its set is accepting.

`ENDS_IN_BA_NFA` accepts strings over `{a, b}` ending in `ba`. `q0` is start, `q2` accepts. `q0` on `a` stays `q0`; on `b` branches to `q0` and `q1`. `q1` on `a` goes to `q2` (the `ba` pattern completes).
Run it. `subset_construction` is called on the NFA.
`start` is `frozenset({'q0'})`. The worklist begins with this single set.
First iteration processes `{q0}`. Alphabet is `{'a', 'b'}`. On `a`, `next_set = {q0}`. On `b`, `next_set = {q0, q1}`  -  a new state added to worklist.
Next iteration processes `{q0, q1}`. On `a`: `q0`→`q0`, `q1`→`q2` gives `{q0, q2}` (new, added). On `b`: `q0`→`{q0, q1}`, `q1` has no `b` gives `{q0, q1}` (self-loop).
Processes `{q0, q2}`. On `a`: `q0`→`q0`, `q2` has no `a` gives `{q0}`. On `b`: `q0`→`{q0, q1}`, `q2` has no `b` gives `{q0, q1}`. Worklist empties.
`dfa_accept` finds `{q0, q2}` contains `q2`, so only that set is accepting. The print shows 3 DFA states with transitions.
Verification runs test strings through the constructed DFA. `ba`, `bba`, `baba` are accepted (end in `ba`); `ab`, `b`, `a`, `''` are rejected.

title: Subset Construction: NFA to DFA
